findings.title: Billable count includes archived projects, so customers are overcharged
findings.explanation: The query counts every project row for the org and has no `archived_at IS NULL` filter. Archiving is a soft delete: `src/routes/projects.ts:49` sets `archived_at`, and `activeProjectNames` in the same file excludes archived rows. Under per-project pricing, an org would be billed for every project it ever archived. The count would also disagree with the project list shown in the UI. Add `AND archived_at IS NULL`, unless product explicitly decides archived projects are billable. If they are, document that decision in a comment and a test. Ideally, share one 'active project' predicate with `activeProjectNames` so the two cannot drift.

findings.title: No tests for the new billing function
findings.explanation: This number feeds invoices directly. Add tests covering an org with no projects, an org with archived projects, and an org that has projects alongside other orgs' projects (tenant isolation). A test with archived projects would have caught the issue above.

findings.title: Count is a point-in-time value with no billing-period semantics
findings.explanation: The function returns the current count. Per-project pricing may need the count as of the period end, or a peak or prorated value. A project created and archived mid-period would otherwise be missed or double-counted. Confirm with the invoice generator that a live snapshot is the intended behavior, and consider accepting an `asOf` or period parameter.
